meta.voice: Skater-to-skater. Plain, confident, a little dry. Never corporate, never hype-y, no exclamation marks. Short sentences. Talk about skating first, the app second.
rules: NEVER invent statistics, download counts, user numbers, or research claims. Only use figures pulled from real App Store Connect data.
Lead with the skating insight; mention BOLTS at most once in the body.
Captions: hook line, 2-4 short lines of substance, one CTA. Under 150 words.
CTA rotates: App Store link in bio / try it free / what's your answer (for community posts).
8-12 hashtags, mixed reach: 3-4 broad, 4-5 mid, 2-3 niche.
No emoji spam. At most one, and only if it genuinely lands.

topics.kicker: The hard part isn't landing it
topics.headline:
It's remembering
you landed it.
topics.sub: Six months of sessions blur together. A logged trick doesn't.
topics.captionSeed: Memory is the weakest part of progression. You land something clean on a Tuesday, and by the next month you genuinely can't remember whether you ever got it. Logging turns skating from a vibe into a record.

topics.headline:
Three ways to
stop plateauing.
items: Pick one trick for the week. Not five.
Log the attempts, not just the makes — that's where the pattern is.
Go back to the last trick you landed. Warm up on a win.
topics.captionSeed: Plateaus are usually a focus problem, not a talent problem. Spreading a session across five tricks means five tricks that all stay at 60%.

topics.headline:
Your session,
by the numbers.
topics.sub: Every trick sorted by type, difficulty and spot — automatically.
topics.captionSeed: You log what you did. BOLTS handles the sorting — by trick type, by difficulty, by spot. The point is to see shape in your skating you'd otherwise miss.

topics.kicker: Two words that hide real progress
topics.headline:
"Almost
had it."
topics.sub: Almost is a feeling. A logged attempt is data you can actually use.
topics.captionSeed: Every skater says it. The problem is 'almost' feels identical whether you're two sessions away or twenty. Attempts logged over time tell you which one it is.

topics.headline:
What was the
first trick
you ever landed?
topics.sub: And roughly how long did it take you to get it?
topics.captionSeed: Everyone remembers the first one. Ollie, shuvit, boardslide — whatever it was, it's the trick that made you think you could actually do this.

topics.headline:
Streaks that
actually mean something.
topics.captionSeed: Most streak counters reward opening an app. This one only moves when you actually skate.

topics.headline:
Log the
bad ones too.
topics.sub: A month later they're the context that makes the good ones make sense.
topics.captionSeed: Nobody wants to record a session where they landed nothing. But those are the sessions that explain the breakthrough three weeks later.

topics.headline:
How to open
a session.
items: Roll for five minutes before you try anything.
Land three tricks you already own.
Then, and only then, go at the new one.
topics.captionSeed: Going straight at your hardest trick cold is how you burn a whole session and your ankles. Warm up on things you can already do.

topics.headline:
Some tricks only
work at one spot.
topics.sub: Log where you landed it, and the pattern shows up fast.
topics.captionSeed: Tracking spots sounds trivial until you notice you've never once landed a trick anywhere but your home park. That's useful to know.

topics.headline:
Make the goal
smaller.
items: "Land a kickflip" is a season. "Get the flick consistent" is a session.
Break the trick into the part you're actually failing.
Give it a deadline you'd be slightly embarrassed to miss.
topics.captionSeed: Big trick goals stall because there's no way to tell if today went well. Shrink the goal until a single session can move it.

topics.kicker: Landing it once isn't landing it
topics.headline:
You own a trick
when you can
call it.
topics.sub: One make is luck. Ten makes across three sessions is a trick.
topics.captionSeed: There's a gap between landing something and having it. The test is whether you can do it on demand, cold, in front of someone.

topics.headline:
Hardest trick
you've ever
actually landed?
topics.sub: No aspirational answers. Only ones you've genuinely got.
topics.captionSeed: Not the trick you're working on. The hardest one that's actually yours.

topics.headline:
Open it and
start logging.
topics.sub: No account, no email, no onboarding carousel. Free on iOS.
topics.captionSeed: You shouldn't have to make an account to write down that you landed a kickflip. Open BOLTS and log it.

topics.headline:
Progress is
invisible
at this range.
topics.sub: Day to day it's noise. Across three months it's obvious.
topics.captionSeed: The reason skating feels like you're not improving is that you're sampling it daily. Zoom out to a season and the line is clear.

topics.headline:
Getting it back
after time off.
items: Expect two sessions of feeling like a beginner. It passes.
Start from the trick you had most locked in, not the newest one.
Check your log — you've done this before, and it's written down.
topics.captionSeed: Time off is brutal on confidence more than ability. A log helps because it's proof you already did the hard part once.

topics.kicker: You don't need a full part
topics.headline:
Most skating
never gets
filmed.
topics.sub: That doesn't mean it didn't count. Write it down instead.
topics.captionSeed: Not every session deserves a camera. But the tricks still happened, and they're still yours. A log is the low-effort version of a part.

topics.headline:
Rate the trick,
not the day.
topics.sub: Difficulty tagging shows you what you're actually pushing.
topics.captionSeed: If almost everything in your log is easy, that's not a bad session — it's a signal about what you've been avoiding.

topics.headline:
Do you skate
better alone
or with people?
topics.sub: And has that changed since you started?
topics.captionSeed: Some people need the push. Some people need nobody watching while they eat it forty times. Curious which way this lands.

topics.headline:
When you keep
bailing early.
items: Roll slower than feels right. Speed is usually not the issue.
Land the trick rolling away in your head first, ten times.
Wear the pads. Commitment is cheaper when the fall is.
topics.captionSeed: Bailing isn't a physical failure, it's a decision your body makes a quarter second early. Reduce the cost of the fall and the decision changes.

topics.headline:
Log it
before
you drive home.
topics.sub: Do it in the car park. By tonight you'll have lost the detail.
topics.captionSeed: The window where you remember exactly what worked is about ten minutes wide. Log in the car park, not at midnight.

topics.kicker: REPLACE WITH REAL APP STORE CONNECT FIGURE
topics.headline: Placeholder milestone card.
topics.sub: Only publish this layout with a verified number.
topics.captionSeed: MILESTONE POSTS REQUIRE REAL DATA. Pull the figure from App Store Connect before using this template. Never estimate.

topics.headline:
You're comparing
your session to
someone's best clip.
topics.sub: Compare it to your own log from six months ago instead.
topics.captionSeed: Every clip you see is the one make out of ninety tries. The only fair comparison is you, earlier.

topics.headline:
What to put on
your list.
items: One trick you're close to. That's the session's work.
One trick that's clearly too hard. That's the direction.
One trick you already have. That's the warm-up and the confidence.
topics.captionSeed: A good trick list has three tiers, not fifteen entries. Close, far, and owned.

topics.headline:
Built because
the notes app
wasn't cutting it.
topics.sub: One skater, one iOS app, no venture money.
topics.captionSeed: BOLTS started as a note on a phone that got too long to be useful. Turns out a lot of skaters have that same note.
